chapters.kicker: The prayer book of the Bible
lines: The Psalms are the prayer book of the Bible: a hundred and fifty poems.
Other parts of the Bible are God's word to his people. The Psalms are also his people's words to him, which he has taken into Scripture.

scripture.text: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him.

lines: They aren't one long list. Two gateway psalms open the collection. Five books follow. And five psalms of Hallelujah close it.
Each of the first four books ends with a short blessing of God.

scripture.text: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.

lines: The largest group of psalms are laments. They complain to God about enemies, about guilt, and about God's own apparent absence, and they do it inside the covenant.
How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?
Most turn toward trust. A few, like Psalm eighty-eight, never do. Protest can be a form of faith.

scripture.text: How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?

lines: Praise in the Psalms is a response. To God's work in creation. To his rescue of Israel. To his help in one crisis.
One person's rescue becomes the whole community's reason to worship.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!

scripture.text: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!

lines: Under every lament and every hymn lies one conviction: the LORD reigns.
Book Three ends by asking how God's covenant with David can stand when the crown lies in the dust. Book Four answers by proclaiming that the LORD is king.

scripture.text: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the prayers of Jesus
lines: The Gospels show Jesus praying the psalms in his suffering. From the cross he cries the opening of Psalm twenty-two.
My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?
Christians since the early church have prayed the Psalms both as their own prayers and as the prayers of Christ.

scripture.text: My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?

lines: Start at the gateway, with Psalm one. The key psalms are one, two, twenty-two, twenty-three, fifty-one, seventy-three, eighty-nine, and a hundred and ten.
Read each one whole, slowly, and out loud.
